nodes.title: A Multimodal Approach To Detect User’s Emotion
nodes.dataset: User reviews, ISEAR dataset (7666 sentences), and pre-classified test samples with positive/negative product reviews.
nodes.methodology: The methodology combines keystroke dynamics (session time, latency, held time, pause rate, capitalization rate, typing speed, error frequency), text analysis using JAWS and NLTK for semantic analysis, and heart rate variation detected via webcam-based photoplethysmography (PPG).
nodes.contribution: Proposes a multimodal approach combining keystroke dynamics, text semantics, and heart rate variation for emotion recognition, with NLTK outperforming JAWS in text analysis.

nodes.dataset: 300 users (45% female, 55% male) with varying demographics, typing tasks, and emotional state self-reports mapped to keyboard behaviors.
nodes.methodology: Empirical study with 300 participants, analyzing typing patterns (speed, backspaces, keystroke duration) using WEKA classifiers to correlate behavioral data with emotional states.
nodes.contribution: Proposes a framework using keyboard stroke patterns for emotion recognition, demonstrating classifiers' effectiveness in distinguishing emotional states through behavioral data.

nodes.title: Does Keystroke Dynamics tell us about Emotions? A Systematic Literature Review and Dataset Construction
nodes.dataset: An interactive web application was developed to construct a new dataset for emotion recognition via keystroke dynamics, addressing the scarcity of existing datasets.
nodes.methodology: A Systematic Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following Kitchenham and Charters' guidelines, involving planning, conducting, and reporting phases with defined inclusion/exclusion criteria.
nodes.contribution: The paper provides a comprehensive SLR of keystroke dynamics in emotion recognition, identifies research gaps, and introduces a new dataset construction framework.

nodes.title: Evaluating Effectiveness of Smartphone Typing as an Indicator of User Emotion
nodes.dataset: Data collected from 22 participants using TapSense, capturing typing features and self-reported emotion labels via Experience Sampling Method (ESM).
nodes.methodology: Qualitative and experimental approach combining online surveys, instrumented keyboard development, and in-the-wild field studies with 22 participants over 3 weeks.
nodes.contribution: Design of TapSense system and analysis demonstrating typing speed as the most discriminative feature for emotion detection from smartphone typing.

nodes.title: Keystroke/Mouse Usage Based Emotion Detection and User Identiﬁcation
nodes.dataset: Custom survey with 35 participants, collecting keystroke and mouse interaction data under induced emotional states.
nodes.methodology: Emotional states were induced via multimedia stimuli. Keystroke and mouse data were collected through a custom survey. Classifiers (KNN, RandomCommittee, RandomForest, Bounded K-means Clustering) analyzed the data for emotional state classification.
nodes.contribution: Proposed Bounded K-means Clustering classifier for emotion detection. Analyzed user identification challenges under emotional state impacts. Demonstrated feasibility of emotion detection from keystroke dynamics.
